    Receiving this email was a surreal milestone. Seeing an Amazon SDE-1 assessment invite for a role with a ~₹54 LPA CTC arrive in my inbox was the exact moment I realized: I am in the arena. 🚀

    Navigating the rigorous Amazon SDE-1 selection pipeline is the ultimate masterclass in what Tier-1 tech companies demand. Experiencing this standard completely redefines your understanding of preparation and exposes the exact blueprint required at the highest levels of engineering.

    Here is the full anatomy of a top-tier SDE-1 selection process, and what it truly takes to crack each phase:

    🔹 PHASE 1: THE MULTI-STAGE ONLINE ASSESSMENT :
This assessment goes beyond a standard coding test; it is a comprehensive, strictly timed evaluation segmented into four distinct sections:
• Section 1: Two DSA coding questions testing pattern recognition (70 mins).
• Section 2: Workplace Judgment / Situational Judgement Test (~15–20 mins).
• Section 3: Business Case / Trade-off Evaluation (~15–20 mins).
• Section 4: Work Style Assessment (~10–20 mins).
A strong foundation in algorithms (Trees, Graphs, Binary Search) is essential, alongside demonstrating behavioral alignment and clear decision-making.

    🔹Phase 2: Core DSA & Architecture (Technical Interview 1) : Writing syntax isn't enough. You have to write highly optimized code without a standard IDE, perform manual dry runs, and heavily defend the deep architecture of every project on your resume.

    🔹Phase 3: Low-Level Design (Technical Interview 2) : Moving beyond basic arrays to highly scalable systems. This round tests your ability to use optimized data structures (like HashMaps) to design real-world applications—like real-time data streaming services—and clearly communicate architectural trade-offs.

    🔹Phase 4: The Bar Raiser (The Veto - Interview 3) : The ultimate cultural test. It’s not enough to be a great coder; you must prove you embody the 14 Leadership Principles—like taking extreme ownership and successfully resolving technical conflicts—while proving you raise the standard of the current engineering floor.

    Regardless of the final outcome of any single application, experiencing this standard of evaluation changes how you approach software engineering forever.

    The benchmark has been set. It’s no longer about just writing code; it’s about absolute mastery of Core CS, System Design, and production-grade projects. Time to keep building. 💻☕

    Posted by Bugfree users (High-Score Interview Experience): A semi-new grad shared a 3-hour Amazon SDE1 virtual onsite. R1: Hiring Manager—LPs via STAR + design/code a file-search API with sorting (name/size) and edge cases. R2: Bar Raiser—LPs then a robot path problem recognized as NP-Hard (TSP-like); brute-force backtracking implemented, but DP+bitmask optimization (LeetCode 847 style) likely expected. R3: SDE2—LPs + medium tree solved in O(n) recursion. Outcome: rejection, but strong lessons on LP storytelling + recognizing when to pivot to optimized DP.     Recently took Amazon's SDE 1 Online Assessment and thought I'd share my experience.

    The first part was the coding round.

    Not gonna lie, it was pretty tough. I got a TLE on one of the test cases at first and thought I had messed it up. After spending some more time optimizing the solution, I was able to get it accepted. Definitely a reminder that getting the logic right isn't always enough, efficiency matters.

    The next part was an AI-assisted coding assessment.

    This was actually the most interesting section for me. It felt less like a coding interview and more like actual development work. You get some code, have to understand what's going on, find the bugs, and fix them.

    A lot of people think the AI will do the work for you, but that wasn't my experience. It was helpful for small things like syntax, API references, HTTP status codes, etc. But when it came to understanding the bug and figuring out the right fix, you still had to do that yourself.

    The last section was the usual Amazon Work Style Assessment.

    Overall, I liked that the OA wasn't just LeetCode. It tested coding, debugging, and how you approach real engineering tasks.

    One thing I found interesting is that even with AI tools available, strong fundamentals still matter a lot. The AI can help, but it can't replace understanding the problem.

    For those who have taken Amazon's OA recently, what was the toughest part for you?

    Preparing for SDE II role: Here’s a 3 month study plan -

    Agar aapka sapna hai ki Google, Facebook, ya Amazon mein SDE-2 role jeetna, toh yeh 3-month ka study plan aapke liye hai!

    📍 Month 1: Build Strong Foundations in DSA
1. Week 1-2:
👉 Arrays, Strings, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues
👉 Trees and Graphs

    2. Week 3-4:
👉 Dynamic Programming
👉 Sorting, Searching, Divide and Conquer

    📍 Month 2: Build Problem Solving speed and accuracy
1. Week 1-2:
👉 Mock interview practice
👉 2 easy, 3 medium, 1 hard LeetCode problem
👉 Graph Traversal
👉 Backtracking
👉 Advanced DP

    2. Week 3-4:
👉 System Design Basics
👉 Small Projects like designing an e-commerce search system

    📍 Month 3: Polish and Simulate real interviews
1. Week 1-2:
👉 Behavioural Questions
👉 Use star to structure responses
👉 Mock behavioural interviews

    2. Week 3:
👉 Revise challenging DSA problems
👉 Read feedback from mock interviews

    3. Week 4:
👉 Mock interviews and feedbacks

    And there you have it folks, use it and thank me later!
This plan has everything you need to not just prepare but excel in interviews!
